1. Core Clinical Tension: A 62-year-old woman presenting with headache, progressive memory decline (MMSE 10/30), gait ataxia, and urinary incontinence developing over several months, accompanied by short shuffling gait and cogwheel rigidity. The clinical picture mimics idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (Hakim-Adams triad) or an atypical neurodegenerative parkinsonian syndrome. The tension is recognizing that intraventricular and cisternal multiloculated racemose cysticercal cysts lacking a visible scolex can produce mechanical non-communicating obstructive hydrocephalus causing reversible subcortical dementia.
2. Admission Breakpoint: Admission triage ends following neurological exam (MMSE 10/30, cogwheel rigidity, brisk reflexes, shuffling gait) and baseline laboratories (normal hemogram and biochemistry). Confirmatory evaluation begins with brain MRI and CSF/serum enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) testing.
3. Differential Distinctions: Idiopathic Normal Pressure Hydrocephalus (iNPH) was the primary clinical mimic given the complete triad of dementia, gait disturbance, and urinary incontinence, but MRI revealed non-communicating obstructive hydrocephalus caused by an obstructing third-ventricular cyst. Primary neurodegenerative dementia / Parkinsonism was ruled out by the acute-on-chronic progression, structural ventricular obstruction, positive serology, and rapid reversal of cognitive and motor deficits (MMSE improving from 10 to 22 within 6 days) post-shunting. Neurocysticercosis is confirmed by cisternal/intraventricular racemose cysts on MRI and strongly positive serum and CSF IgG ELISA titers.
case_prompt:
A 62-year-old woman presented with an eight-month history of persistent headache, general slowness in activities of daily living, and progressive memory disturbances. Over the preceding six months, her symptoms worsened with gait instability, pronounced psychomotor slowing, and new-onset urinary incontinence.

On physical examination, she was afebrile and hemodynamically stable. General and systemic physical examinations were unremarkable. Higher mental function testing revealed severe cognitive impairment, with a Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE) score of 10 out of 30, with prominent deficits in executive function, recent memory, visuospatial skills, and calculation. Cranial nerves were intact, and funduscopic examination showed no papilledema. Motor examination revealed increased muscle tone throughout all four extremities with bilateral cogwheel rigidity. Motor power was preserved (5/5) and deep tendon reflexes were brisk with bilateral flexor plantar responses. Sensory examination was normal. She walked with a short, slow, shuffling gait. Initial complete blood count and routine biochemical panels were completely within normal limits.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The patient presented with the classic triad of gait impairment, urinary incontinence, and dementia, but neuroimaging revealed non-communicating obstructive hydrocephalus due to an obstructing intraventricular cystic lesion rather than communicating ventriculomegaly.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: There was obstructive hydrocephalus with dilatation of lateral ventricles and third ventricle. Fourth ventricle was not dilated and cause of hydrocephalus was cyst in the third ventricle.

diagnostic_reasoning.candidate: Primary Neurodegenerative Parkinsonian Dementia / Lewy Body Disease
diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: Parkinsonian features including cogwheel rigidity and shuffling gait suggested a neurodegenerative parkinsonian dementia, but this was excluded by the structural obstructive hydrocephalus and dramatic cognitive recovery (MMSE improving to 22/30) immediately following ventriculoperitoneal shunting.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: Post shunting, she had significant improvement in her cognitive status, with MMSE improving to 22/30 at the time of discharge 6 days post shunting.

diagnostic_reasoning.rule_out_reason: The diagnosis was confirmed by brain MRI demonstrating multilocular, racemose conglomerate cystic lesions in the Sylvian fissure, basal cisterns, and third ventricle, corroborated by strongly positive serum and CSF IgG ELISA titers for neurocysticercosis.
diagnostic_reasoning.quote: NCC serology (ELISA for IgG antibodies) in serum and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) was positive with titers of 1:1600 and 1:80, respectively.

editor_comments: Case prompt strictly redacted of pathogen names and imaging findings. Breakpoint placed before brain MRI and serological testing.
